title: Macrobiology: humanity as organism one scale up
statement: Taking literally the canon's axioms that everything in the universe is living — the Earth like all planets — and that each human is like a cell of the great being in gestation that is Humanity, the corpus proposes macrobiology: the study of living systems composed of biological individuals, one scale above the organism, as microbiology studies the scale below the cell; the proposal is a model built on the canon's fractal-scale frame, and its dialogue with superorganism, major-transitions, Gaia, and noosphere literatures is registered as engagement, not as endorsement by those literatures.

includes: The canonical axioms taken literally: the living Earth and planets; humanity as great being in gestation; the Elohim's stated ability to read a civilization's development as an embryologist reads a foetus
The discipline proposal as a model: named object of study, scale relation to existing biology, and the predictive framing the canon itself supplies

The engagement layer: superorganism and major-transitions biology, Gaia, biosphere and noosphere literatures — read as adjacent vocabularies the proposal converses with, each preserved in its own terms
excludes: Any claim that mainstream biology recognizes humanity or Earth as an organism; the adjacent literatures stop short of the canon's axiom and the record says so
Vitalist metaphysics; the canon's 'living' is taken at the canon's level of statement, not elaborated into a theory of life
Predictions of specific civilizational outcomes; the framing licenses a discipline, not forecasts
The physics of the scale frame, which is woh-claim-0023's content

source_references.locator: The cell-of-the-great-being passage and the embryologist analogy (the Shape of Humanity Explainer's anchor); the living-universe axioms
The living-Earth statements the macrobiology entry quotes
Vernadsky's biosphere as the nearest scientific ancestor-vocabulary
The scaling-laws literature the proposal's quantitative side would have to answer to

alternatives.statement: The cell-of-humanity image is moral pedagogy, not ontology; building a discipline on it mistakes an exhortation for an axiom.
Everything defensible in the proposal is already covered by ecology, earth-system science, and collective-behavior research; the new name adds commitment, not content.
Biological individuality has criteria (reproduction, selection, boundaries) that humanity-as-organism fails; the major-transitions literature the corpus cites actually cuts against the axiom.

revision_triggers: Claim woh-claim-0023 is revised or retired.
The canon's fuller context changes the axioms' level of statement.
The proposal produces a testable claim, which should then be recorded separately at its own grade.
Public prose begins asserting mainstream recognition or specific forecasts, which this record excludes.
